main_text.p: su[?] nostro proposito loquimur de privatis vim nobis inferen-tibus, quibus impunè nosmet opponimus, ut, si fuga tuta non sit aut salutaris, recte[?] nostrum locum tueamur, injuriam pro-pulsaturi.

Tiraq. de Nobil.c. 20. n.63. aliique ibidem.Neque tamen hic audiendi Doctores, qui distinguunt inter plebejos & nobiles. Inter rusticos & milites, quasi hisce Gilhauf. Arbor. Crim.c. 2. tit.12. n.36[?]fuga sit ignominiosa, adeoque fugere non debent, illis non item. Et quia circa necessa-Constit. crim.Carol. art. 140.riam defensionem, quæ juris est naturæ, idem propulsatio1. 3. D. just. & jur. § jus autem gentium.nis modus in omnibus adhibendus est: quod illud jus non distinguat inter rusticos & milites, plebejos & nobiles. Ut fruftra nos aliquam distinctionem adhiberi velimus. Instit.jur. nat.gent. civil.Init. Instit. in fin. de libertin.Et quia nulla ignominia eum manere potest, qui maluit ad tempus cedere furenti. page.notes: The first word of the page is doubtful (possibly "in" or "su"); "recte" is read from a worn letter. The last margin reference is partly cut off at the foot of the visible part and is marked [?]. The first two lines of the page are set in roman, with the paragraph continuing from the previous page. The first note's top word is cut off at the top of the scan and is read as "Constit." with uncertainty; the final word of the last note is doubtful ("libertin." may be "bertin." with a superscript). The last line ends with "ab", which is printed as the start of the next line on the cut-off part of the page.
